headline.en: A long note isn't about big lungs. It's letting the air out slowly, and stopping while it's still easy.

detail.en: Hum a few slow slides, low to high and back
Belly, sides and back widen; shoulders stay down
Never squeeze out the last drop

text.en: Hold "oo" over the drone as long as it's easy. No goal: this first hold is your own starting point.
Again, with your first try marked. Breathe low, let the air out slowly, and stop while it's still steady.

measures.en: Your stars are for how your note ended (steady, because you stopped while it was easy), how steady it was, and reaching your own goal. Going past it earns nothing more.

headline.en: Good support slows your ribs from collapsing. Singers call it appoggio: leaning.

detail.en: At your sides, thumbs to the back
Feel the ribs widen; shoulders stay down
As you sing, let them close slowly

text.en: Try a big breath (not your biggest) and sing at once, without holding it. Then a normal breath. Which felt easier?
Hands on your ribs. Hold "vv" to your goal, keeping the ribs wide. Did your shoulders stay down?

measures.en: Your stars are for how the hold ended, how steady it was, and reaching your goal. Whether your ribs stayed wide is yours to check: we can't see it.

headline.en: In songs, the long notes come at the ends of lines. Plan the air so the end stays steady.

detail.en: Not all on the first word

text.en: Swing Low, Sweet Chariot, slowly, with the guide. Breathe before "Coming".
Now on your own, over its chords. Keep "home" steady to its end.

measures.en: Your stars are for where the line's notes landed, and for "home" staying steady to its end.

headline.en: A little longer than your first hold, still ending on purpose.

detail.en: Two seconds past your first hold

text.en: Hold "oo" over the drone to your new goal. Your first hold is marked.

measures.en: Your stars are for how the hold ended, how steady it was, and reaching your goal: your first hold plus two seconds.

headline.en: A buzz shows whether your air comes out evenly. Uneven air, uneven buzz.

detail.en: "vv", "zz", "mm", or a lip or tongue trill
Keep the air flowing and the lips loose; fingertips at your cheeks help
Like a steady breeze, not a gust

text.en: Hold your buzz over the drone to your goal: "vv", "zz", "mm" or a trill, your pick. Stop while it's even.

measures.en: Your stars are for how the buzz ended, how steady it was, and reaching your goal. Whether a trill really bubbled is yours to hear: we hear only its pitch.

headline.en: The air stays even while the pitch moves: up five notes and back, in one breath.

text.en: With the guide: up from do to so and back, on a trill or "vv", in one breath.
Now on your own, in one breath. Keep the buzz even, up and down.

measures.en: Your stars are for every note of the hill landing close to its middle while you kept the buzz going.

headline.en: The end of a breath lets pitch fall. Plan the ending instead: stop on time, while it's steady.

text.en: Listen to each, as often as you like, then choose.

prompt.en: Which one ran out of air?

why.en: B sags at its end: the air ran out. A stops on purpose, still steady.
B stops while it's steady. A drops at the end.

prompt.en: Which one ran out of air?

why.en: A falls in its last moment. That's the sound to avoid: stop a little sooner.
A: steady to its very end.

text.en: Hold do for six beats with the guide, and stop with it.
On your own: hold do for six beats over the drone and stop exactly at the end, still steady.

measures.en: Your stars are for stopping on time (within about a tenth of a second of the end) and for the note staying steady to its end.

headline.en: Three long holds that stack into a chord: do, then mi over your do, then so over both.

detail.en: An easy eight seconds, as at the start
Do, mi, so, one at a time

text.en: Then and now: hold "oo" for an easy eight seconds. Your first hold is marked.

headline.en: Breathe normally for a few breaths. Then your chord, one note at a time.

text.en: Hold do over the drone, easy and steady.
Now mi, three up, over your own do.
Now so, five up, over your do and mi: your chord.

measures.en: Your stars are for how your so ended and how steady it was. Listen back: the chord is all you.

headline.en: Breathe in, then let the breath turn straight into the note, with no hold. Think an "h", don't sing it.

detail.en: A pause there usually means a closed throat
The tone starts from moving air
Whispering can tire the voice more

text.en: Listen to each start, as often as you like, then choose. A hard start is only for hearing, never for practising.

prompt.en: Which one started right on its note?

why.en: A slides up into the note. B starts right on it.
A lets air out before the tone: breathy. B turns straight into the note.
B starts with a click in the throat: a hard start. A is smooth.
A little click at the start: hard.
A puff of air before the tone: breathy.

prompt.en: Which one started right on its note?

why.en: A starts on it; B scoops up from below.

text.en: Six "ah"s, a breath before each, the breath turning straight into the note. Was each start balanced, breathy or hard? That's yours to hear: we hear the pitch.

measures.en: Your stars are for each start being on its pitch from the first moment. Whether it was balanced is yours to judge: we can't hear that yet.

headline.en: Short notes start with a small bounce low in the belly. The throat stays open.

detail.en: Low in the belly, like a little laugh

text.en: "Ha" on each note, short and bouncy: listen, then echo. Do, mi, so, mi, do.

measures.en: Your stars are for every short note landing close to its pitch from its first moment.

headline.en: The French tune Mozart wrote twelve variations on, known in English as Twinkle, Twinkle: each note on the breath, the last one held.

text.en: Then and now: hold "oo" for an easy eight seconds. Your first hold is marked.
With the guide: short "dah"s, a breath at the halfway, the last note held.
On your own now. Each note on the breath, and hold the last one steady.

measures.en: Your stars are for every note starting on its pitch, and the last one held steady to its end.
